page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 360 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it lacks GPU acceleration.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-96 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core and Geekbench text processing. It also achieves top-tier status in static web serving throughput at 126.92 GB/sec and Passmark CPU encryption at 87093.55. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 538.12 GB/sec, and the system processes 4350.33 tokens/sec in LLM inference for small models. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Passmark memory scores falling in the average middle 50% tier.

From a resource density perspective, the c4-standard-96 offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for high-density workloads without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. The server is highly effective for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
